audio_caption: The audio begins with a musical piece in the style of Christian rock or gospel, creating a worshipful mood. Transitioning from this musical backdrop, a male voice speaks in a calm and reassuring tone, explaining that they're about to start on an axillary abscess on a young patient who has been in pain for several days. He mentions an ultrasound showing a solid and cystic component in the area, and explains that they will drain it today and provide antibiotics. The male speaker then addresses the patient directly, reassuring her they're going to start with some numbing medicine. The music fades slightly as he praises her by saying “good job.” He again asks the patient if she is okay.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker stating that burning will go away in a couple of minutes. The sound of rustling fabric is then heard.  The male speaker then describes two drapes covering someone, explaining one is sticky and one is blue to cover the body and keep the area sterile.

The audio features a male speaker discussing a medical condition, specifically an abscess, and expressing doubt about needing a hospital visit, even though it's causing significant pain and limited arm movement. He asks someone if they are doing okay and assures them the procedure won't be too bothersome. There's a mention of pus being expelled, indicating a potential lancing procedure. This dialog is interspersed with sounds of squishing, consistent with squeezing or cleaning a wound.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker stating they will culture something and send it to the lab for testing, expressing the hope that the individual will feel better. The speaker then confirms they see a lot of pus in the area, and asks if the individual is okay.

The audio clip contains speech from a male individual, who seems to be giving comfort, saying, "we can squeeze the pus out of there. There's still much pus. Feeling any better?" He suggests that the removal of the pus will make the recipient feel better. Interspersed with the speech is the sound of squeezing.

The audio clip features speech, with a male speaker explaining that "because of this skin and this area is very tightly comparted" any increase in size or volume causes a lot of pressure. He also says, "I'm sorry honey, almost done sweetie, almost done," in a gentle tone. This takes place against a backdrop of gentle humming.

The clip opens with a male speaker, sounding clinical, discussing an "infected sebaceous" issue and mentions that they are going to start it with a "pathology." He notes a "cyst" that got infected, and then asks the patient if it hurts. He then comments that this is an infected cyst, and says they will add more numbing medicine to try to clean it out. A male voice checks in to ask how the patient is doing, followed by sounds of medical instruments. He describes trying to clean out the cyst's wall as much as possible because it had already ruptured, expressing concern about recurrence. He reassures her that she's doing great and is brave, and then expresses approval. He declares that it looks pretty clean now inside.

The clip features a male speaker discussing wound care, noting that a "wet dressing is usually better than soaked gauze" initially, followed by a transition to "regular saline soaked or dry gauze," depending on the wound's appearance. His tone is informative and calm.  There are no other sound events.

The audio clip begins with a male speaker mentioning "the pegging is really tight, so if there's any oozing or stuff, it can stop." He then notes things get "much easier" after that. The speaker concludes by stating they are "just about done with this case," draining an "axillary abscess" from an "infected sebaceous cyst" under local anesthesia, and that the patient "has done very well." He states that she can go home, eat and drink, and take some antibiotics. The audio ends with a high-pitched sound, possibly a medical device.
